summary: Prioritize the Log4j upgrade; assess BEAST through TLS configuration rather than the OpenSSL version alone.
coverageNotes: Reviewed audit.json only; no web research or runtime verification performed.

findings.reasoning: Log4j-core 2.14.1 is affected by Log4Shell when attacker-controlled data reaches vulnerable lookup processing, but 2.15.0 is an inadequate upgrade target because subsequent Log4j vulnerabilities require further fixes.
evidence: audit.json identifies log4j-core 2.14.1 in /srv/shop and marks CVE-2021-44228 as known exploited.
fix: Upgrade to a maintained, Java-compatible Log4j release, using 2.17.1 as a minimum baseline for Java 8 or later, then restart shop.service.

corrections.new: Maintained Java-compatible release; minimum baseline 2.17.1 for Java 8+
corrections.why: 2.15.0 addresses the original CVE but leaves subsequent Log4j vulnerabilities.

findings.reasoning: BEAST depends on vulnerable SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0 CBC usage and client behavior, so OpenSSL 3.0.15 alone neither establishes exposure nor supports the claim that no mitigation exists.
evidence: audit.json supplies an OpenSSL version but no negotiated protocols, cipher suites, or client behavior.
fix: Verify the application's TLS termination configuration and disable SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0, requiring TLS 1.2 or later.

corrections.old: No fix is known for openssl 3.0.15 yet.
corrections.new: Assess protocol and cipher configuration; mitigate by requiring TLS 1.2 or later.
corrections.why: BEAST is a protocol-dependent exposure, not an established unpatched defect in this package version.

actions.title: Remediate /srv/shop

changes.name: log4j-core
changes.to: Maintained Java-compatible release; minimum baseline 2.17.1 for Java 8+

also: Assess proc:bbbb for BEAST exposure through its actual TLS configuration.

steps.text: Upgrade the packages below in /srv/shop: replace log4j-core with a maintained release compatible with the application's Java runtime.
Inspect the application's TLS termination configuration and require TLS 1.2 or later where legacy protocols remain enabled.
Verify application health, the loaded Log4j version, and that the TLS endpoint rejects SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0; reload any separate TLS terminator if its configuration changed.

upstream.note: Log4j fixes exist; current maintained releases were not checked.

actions.why: Preserves the default upgrade-and-restart steps while correcting the Log4j target and replacing the unsupported OpenSSL no-fix claim with configuration assessment.
